title: Làm ơn cho tôi một tô phở
englishTitle: I’d like a bowl of phở, please
pronunciation: Lam on cho toi mot to pho
summary: Keeps the food or drink request clear in a stall, cafe, or busy counter.

sections.title: At a glance
sections.body: Point to the item, menu line, receipt, size, or photo.

sections.title: Quick say
sections.body: Say Làm ơn cho tôi một tô phở as one clean sentence; the menu line, dish photo, bill, or ingredient can carry the exact detail. Point to the item, menu line, receipt, size, or photo.

sections.title: Break it down
sections.body: Hear Làm ơn + cho tôi một as the reference point, then compare it with the full phrase.

sections.title: When to use it
sections.body: At a stall, cafe, or busy counter, keep the menu line, dish photo, table item, or bill visible while the first answer comes back.

phrases.vietnamese: Cho tôi cơm ăn kèm được không?
phrases.english: Can I have rice with this?
phrases.pronunciation: Cho toi com an kem duoc khong

phrases.vietnamese: Cho tôi xin chén súp riêng được không?
phrases.english: Can I have soup on the side?
phrases.pronunciation: Cho toi xin chen sup rieng duoc khong

phrases.vietnamese: Xin vui lòng cho nước sốt vào bên cạnh
phrases.pronunciation: Xin vui long cho nuoc sot vao ben canh

sections.title: Good to know
sections.body: Menus and photos do a lot of work. Point to the item while you say the phrase so the reply can stay short.

sections.title: Explore next
sections.body: Once they answer, listen for whether can I have chili sauce?; can I have napkins?; can I order half a portion? fits the next step.

phrases.vietnamese: Cho tôi xin chanh được không?
phrases.pronunciation: Cho toi xin chanh duoc khong

phrases.vietnamese: Tôi có thể dùng tương ớt được không?
phrases.pronunciation: Toi co the dung tuong ot duoc khong

sections.title: Useful nearby phrases
sections.body: Keep more herbs please; a spoon and chopsticks please; can I have rice with this? ready for the next turn.
